src.text: Turkish coffee (boiled, unfiltered, about 7 g coffee per 70 ml cup) has no USDA record. src.text: Alcohol-free beer: values from the USDA record “Malt beverage, includes non-alcoholic beer” (37 kcal and 8 g sugar per 100 g, 0.3 g alcohol). src.text: Burek: there is no USDA burek, so the values are from a Croatian producer’s cheese burek (Čakovečki mlinovi: 297 kcal, 16 g fat, 3.3 g sugar per 100 g). The web table does not print “per 100 g”, but EU law requires nutrition per 100 g, and the same table format gives a 400 g loaf 222 kcal, which can only be per 100 g. Burek varies: labels range from about 250 to 320 kcal per 100 g.
src.cite: Čakovečki mlinovi, Burek (net weight 150 g; “slojevi tijesta i sirnog nadjeva”, layers of dough and cheese filling): energy 1241 kJ / 297 kcal, fat 16 g, saturates 7.5 g, carbohydrate 29 g, sugars 3.3 g, protein 9.7 g, salt 1.4 g. Basis: Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 Art. 32(2) “shall be expressed per 100 g or per 100 ml”. Range: Sofka beef burek 247 kcal, Lidl meat burek 316 kcal (Open Food Facts 9120018535583, 4056489610953)

src.text: Burek: cheese is a Croatian producer’s label; meat, spinach and potato are our recipes from USDA phyllo, filling and oil in the shares shown on Croatian and Bosnian labels. Real burek varies a lot (labels 247–316 kcal per 100 g).

src.text: Potato burek (krumpiruša) is our recipe for a 150 g piece: 75 g phyllo, 45 g boiled potato, 15 g onion and 15 g sunflower oil (USDA parts), 268 kcal per 100 g. src.text: The base is USDA’s 14-inch chain cheese pizza (dough, tomato sauce, mozzarella): 1 slice = 107 g, the whole pizza 853 g. Blood sugar: the mean of the whole pizzas tested in healthy people (30–56; no plain cheese pizza was tested), Atkinson 2008 and 2021 tables, GI 43.

src.text: Extra cheese on pizza: 6.3 g of mozzarella per slice, USDA’s own recipe for an extra-cheese pizza (41 g of cheese added to a 691 g pizza, 5.9%). src.text: Kebab is our builder: pita or wrap, chicken or beef, vegetables and sauce, each a USDA record. The amounts follow twenty döner kebabs bought and weighed in Italian shops (402 g: 37% meat, 25% bread, 25% vegetables, 13% sauce). Our default has about the study’s measured fat and protein per 100 g. The study’s 226 kcal per 100 g is gross energy from burning the food in a calorimeter; the energy the body can use from its measured protein, fat and starch is about 177–187 kcal per 100 g, and ours is 192. Kebab shops differ a lot, mostly in the meat.
src.cite: Panozzo et al. 2015, Ital J Food Saf 4:4535 (20 weighed döner kebabs); RTL test via Mallorca Revue; USDA FNDDS 2706962 gyro

src.text: Pita: 100 g of bread (USDA white pita). Blood sugar: white pita bread as tested in healthy people (Atkinson 2008 table A1, 68 ± 5), GI 68.

src.text: Chicken: 150 g of meat (roasted chicken thigh with skin, USDA). Twenty döner kebabs bought and weighed in Italy averaged 402 g with 35–40% meat, about 150 g; a German TV test weighed 80–173 g of meat; USDA’s gyro uses 60 g. The study found skin in the döner meat and 8.6 g of fat per 100 g of kebab, which skinless thigh meat cannot reach, so we use thigh with skin.
